verdict.line: You own the lane and the solo-kill angle through level 5, but if the fight drags past level 10 Mundo's health-based scaling claws it back to the 45.7% win rate the data shows over 138 games.

brief.thesis: K'Sante's Q (Ntofo Strikes) stacks into a shockwave pull that Mundo has no tool to escape, and W (Path Maker) stuns him the instant he's locked in — that's the structural reason K'Sante holds lane and solo-kill advantage early. But Dr. Mundo's Adrenaline Rush regenerates a percentage of his max health every second and Masochism (E) scales his AD off missing health, so the longer a trade or skirmish runs, the more those numbers quietly flip the exchange in his favor.

theirWindow.when: Mundo sits below 50% HP baiting a dive
theirWindow.what: Masochism grants him AD scaled to missing health, so his autos hit hardest exactly when he looks killable, and Adrenaline Rush is already regenerating him back. Don't commit a trade on HP bar alone — check whether your Q (Ntofo Strikes) stacks and W (Path Maker) stun are actually up before you dive.

yourWindow.when: You land 2 Q stacks on him in melee
yourWindow.what: The second Ntofo Strikes stack fires a shockwave that pulls Mundo in from up to 450 range, and he has no dash or disengage to answer it. Follow immediately with W (Path Maker) for the stun — this chain is where your measured solo-kill advantage actually comes from.

start.why: Mundo's whole early game is auto-attack and Infected Cleaver poke chipping your max health; the passive damage reduction on autos and the regen let you match his Adrenaline Rush sustain instead of losing the war of attrition before level 6.

boots.why: Masochism (E) is an auto-attack AD steroid, so flat damage reduction on his autos is worth more here than Mercury's Treads' tenacity — his W doesn't disable you, it only shortens his own disable duration.

core.why: The CDR and burst catalyst feed your Q (Ntofo Strikes) stack generation, letting you get to the 2-stack shockwave pull faster in every extended trade.
Grievous Wounds cuts directly into Adrenaline Rush's per-second max-health regen, which is the single stat that lets Mundo win long skirmishes against you.
Stacking resistances off your own tankiness lets you keep forcing fights into the late game, where his Masochism AD spike matters less against your scaling armor and MR.

situational.when: his Adrenaline Rush sustain is already winning trades before level 6
the lane turns into a prolonged poke-and-regen stalemate
the enemy team adds burst magic damage on top of Mundo's physical poke
you're leaning on R (All Out)'s healing to close out extended fights

runes.keystoneWhy: Mundo's trade pattern is about chipping your max health with Infected Cleaver and autos over time; Grasp's bonus health and on-hit sustain directly answers that war of attrition instead of trying to out-burst a champion with built-in self-healing.

summoners.why: Teleport is run in 71% of these games (49.6% win rate) because it lets you reset off Mundo's ranged Q poke and still rejoin skirmishes at full resources; Flash+Ignite (47.9% WR, 27.3% pick) is the better call specifically when you plan to force the level 2-5 solo-kill window off your Q-shockwave into W stun.

playing.title: Build to 2 Q stacks before committing
playing.detail: Ntofo Strikes grants a stack on hit; don't throw W (Path Maker) into a trade until you're one hit away from the 2-stack shockwave pull, since that's what removes his ability to just walk out of range.

playing.title: Don't dive on HP bar alone
playing.detail: A low-health Mundo is baiting you — Masochism scales his AD off missing health and Adrenaline Rush is already ticking him back up. Only commit if your Q stacks and W stun are both available.

playing.title: Push levels 3-5 hard
playing.detail: This is your measured solo-kill window before his sustain items and R (Sadism) at level 6 come online — force fights here, not later.

playing.title: Save E (Footwork) for his Infected Cleaver
playing.detail: His Q is a 975-range skillshot thrown on a 4s cooldown that scales off your max health; use Footwork's shield to blunt the hit or to reposition out of his throw angle entirely.

playing.title: Don't waste R chasing a poke trade
playing.detail: All Out is on a 120/100/80/80/80s cooldown and knocks him through walls before you go All Out on him — save it for a kill setup near a wall, not just to win a single exchange.

playing.title: Prioritize grievous wounds if the sustain race stalls
playing.detail: If Mundo's Adrenaline Rush is outhealing your trades, rushing Bramble Vest into Thornmail cuts his regen directly rather than trying to out-damage a champion built to not die to poke.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, boots, runes, summoner spells, and all win-rate/sample numbers above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the ability breakdowns, trade windows, and tactical reasoning connecting them are my own read of the matchup, not measured data.
